walkthroughs.body_html:
Atom: 1 x 10^-10 m. Nucleus: 10000x smaller.

Almost all mass is in the nucleus; most of the atom is empty space.

Dalton (1803): solid sphere.

Thomson (1897): plum pudding. Rutherford (1911): nuclear model.

Bohr (1913): electrons in fixed energy shells. Chadwick (1932): neutron.

Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass number.

Some are unstable and decay - radioactive.

What did Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment show about the atom?
options: Mass changes with location but weight does not.
It showed that atoms are solid spheres of positive charge with electrons embedded inside.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense positive nucleus.

mcqs.q: In a balanced nuclear equation, what must be equal on both sides?
options: Only the atomic number (proton count) needs to balance.
The total mass number (top numbers) and the total atomic number (bottom numbers) must both balance.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass and weight are the same thing, just expressed in different units.
Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N) and depends on g.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
